notes:
CHR-618/CHR-621 ticket state 7 (zoomed out half). Third pass, after two rounds of CTO correction:

**Round 1 → round 2**: replaced a 42-tile/17%-zoom screen (contradicted its own "Fit all" state) with 186 tiles (Christian's real project size) at an honestly-computed **42% zoom**. Full arithmetic: native tile 180×150px (`$board-tile` `default`: 120px thumb + ~30px name row); board's usable canvas 1356×764px (1440×900 frame minus topbar/toolbar/sidebar-rail chrome minus `$spacing.2xl` grid padding); 17×11 grid (187 cells, one dropped from the partial last row) = 186 tiles; width equation `17w + 16×4px = 1356` → `w ≈ 76px`; `76 ÷ 180 ≈ 42%`. `$board-toolbar`'s `fitall-edgesoff` variant and `$zoom-slider`'s `min` variant readout/thumb were updated to 42% in place (nothing else consumed the old 17% state). This also forced correcting the label-hide threshold from a guessed "<20%" to a legibility-computed "<60%" (`typography.size-xs` drops under ~8px there) — 42% sits inside that revised hidden-label band, so all 186 tiles are name-less.

**Round 3 (this pass)**: the 181 unpinned `$pin-button` `default` markers were pure noise at 42% and buried the five pinned ones, which are the entire point of an overview screen. Removed the unpinned affordance from every non-pinned tile — only the 5 pinned tiles (`bc-8`, `bc-55`, `bc-100`, `bc-150`, `bc-178`) carry a `$pin-button`, always `pinned` variant. The unpinned pin affordance is not gone from the product, just from this static screen: it is hover-revealed at low zoom in the real app, and a static screenshot cannot represent a hover state, so it is correctly omitted here rather than faked. See `$board-tile`'s own `usage` notes for the same rule stated at the component level, and `board-view`/`board-view-presented` (100% zoom) for where the unpinned affordance does render, always-visible, since hover-only behavior is specific to the low-zoom/overview case.

Edges are off (`fitall-edgesoff`), "Fit all" and 42% both active and self-consistent — 186 tiles fill the board's usable canvas edge to edge. The five pinned markers are now the only accent-colored elements on the whole board and read immediately.
